title: Smt. Edvina Samuel vs Abhishek Walter (2025:Rj-Jd:19348) on 21 April, 2025

[2025:RJ-JD:19348]

 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT
 JODHPUR
 S.B. Civil Transfer Appl. No. 190/2024

Smt. Edvina Samuel W/o Shri Abhishek Walter, Aged About 31
Years, D/o Shri Shashi Samuel Resident Of Plot No 66, Sector 4 ,
Navdurga Vihar, Jhalamand, Jodhpur
 ----Petitioner
 Versus
Abhishek Walter S/o Late Shri Sunil Walter, Aged About 34 Years,
Resident Of Plot No 28, Mission Compound, Ajmer Road, Jaipur
 ----Respondent


For Petitioner(s) : None present
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Mahesh Joshi



 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE YOGENDRA KUMAR PUROHIT

1. The instant civil transfer application has been filed by the

petitioner-wife seeking transfer of Case No.165/2024 "Abhishek

Walter Vs. Edvina Samuel" preferred by the respondent-husband

under Section 10 of the Divorce Act seeking divorce pending

before Family Court No.1, Jaipur Metro to the Family Court,

Jodhpur.

2. Vide order dated 24.09.24, notices were directed to be

issued to the respondent and further proceedings in Civil Misc.

Case No. 165/2024 "Abhishek Walter Vs. Edvina Samuel" pending

before Family Court No.1, Jaipur Metro were stayed.

3. None present for the petitioner. Heard learned counsel for

the respondent and perused the material available on record.




 (Downloaded on 24/04/2025 at 09:50:08 PM)

4. It is averred in the transfer petition on behalf of the

petitioner-wife that the marriage between the petitioner-wife and

respondent-husband was solemnized as per Christian rituals on

18.11.2016 at Jodhpur. Since the petitioner-wife was harassed,

maltreated for bringing less dowry and turned out of her

matrimonial home, therefore, she lodged an FIR No.0117/2019 at

P.S. Mahila Thana, District Jodhpur City West for the offences

under Sections 498A , 406 and 323 IPC, in which, challan has been

filed and matter is pending trial before Special Additional Chief

Judicial Magistrate, PCPNDT Cases, Jodhpur Metro. It is also stated

that with a view to harass and humiliate the petitioner, the

respondent-husband has filed an application u/s 10 of the Divorce

Act against the petitioner seeking divorce before learned Family

Court No.1, Jaipur Metro.

5. According to the petitioner, she is a young lady and is

residing at Jodhpur with her parents. She is fully dependent on

her parents. The distance from Jodhpur to Jaipur is 325 kms. It is

very difficult, expensive and onerous for the petitioner to travel

from the place of her residence at Jodhpur to Jaipur to defend the

case instituted by the respondent husband. It is also the stand of

the petitioner-wife that since the aforesaid case filed by the

petitioner-wife is pending at Jodhpur, the case filed by the

respondent-husband pending before Family Court No.1, Jaipur

Metro may be transferred to Family Court, Jodhpur.

6. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent vehemently

opposed the transfer application and prayed to dismiss the same.

7. It is settled law that while considering transfer of case in

matrimonial proceedings instituted by the husband, the

convenience of the wife is to be looked into. In this regard,

recently, Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the matter of N.C.V.

Aishwarya Vs. A.S.Saravana Karthik Sha, (Civil Appeal

No.4894/2022 arising out of SLP (C) No.16465/2021)

decided on 18.7.2022, while considering transfer of matrimonial

case under Section 24 CPC, has observed as under:-

"The cardinal principle for exercise of power under
 Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the
 ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit,
 appeal or other proceeding. In matrimonial matters,
 wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea
 of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration
 the economic soundness of both the parties, the social
 strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern,
 their standard of life prior to the marriage and
 subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the
 parties in eking out their livelihood and under whose
 protective umbrella they are seeking their sustenance
 to life. Given the prevailing socio-economic paradigm
 in the Indian society, generally, it is the wife's
 convenience which must be looked at while
 considering transfer."

8. Having considered the submissions made on behalf of the

respondent and averments made in the transfer petition as also

the material placed on record, looking to the facts and

circumstances of the case noticed above and the settled position

of law by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of N.C.V.

Aishwarya (supra), the transfer application is allowed. It is ordered

that the Case No. 165/2024 pending before Family Court No.1,

Jaipur Metro titled as 'Abhishek Walter Vs. Edvina Samuel" be

transferred to the Family Court No.1, Jodhpur Metro. The Family

Court No.1, Jaipur Metro is directed to send the record of the

 aforesaid case to Family Court No.1, Jodhpur Metro immediately.

 The parties are directed to appear before the Family Court No.1,

 Family Court No.1, Jaipur Metro and Family Court No.1, Jodhpur
